post_topic: The unglamorous production work that separates a live product from one that just looks like it
image_description: Single standalone diagram. One concept only. No panels, no grids, no collages. Full bleed 1080x1080px white background. An iceberg diagram oriented vertically, center-aligned. Above the waterline, a small visible section labeled in bold: 'What people see' — containing one item listed inside: 'The Launch'. Below the waterline, a large submerged section labeled in bold: 'What ships before it's real' — containing four stacked labeled boxes arranged top to bottom: Box 1: 'Real analytics wired in'; Box 2: 'First-touch campaign attribution at signup'; Box 3: 'Branded favicon — no more blank browser tab'; Box 4: 'Metadata bug fix — share previews actually render'. A horizontal wavy line divides the above-water and below-water sections. The waterline label reads 'Visible to users' on the right side. An amber callout arrow points to the submerged section with the label: 'Where production actually happens'. Navy #0A0F1E primary elements, blue #5a96ff highlights, amber #F5A623 callouts and important labels. Clean sans-serif font. Real cloud provider logos where relevant. Small text 'Kelvin Davis' bottom right corner. Professional LinkedIn infographic style similar to ByteByteGo. White background. No dark backgrounds.
